newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels say they captured southern garrison.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say they captured southern garrison.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Saturday they had captured an army garrison west of the southern capital of Juba, bringing to seven the number of outposts taken in two days.
"We captured Amadi garrison on Friday evening. It is one of the important outposts of Juba," said Yassir Arman, spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) in the Eritrean capital Asmara.
"SPLA forces around Juba have captured seven garrisons in the last two days. They continue their advance to Juba," said Arman, adding rebels seized equipment and destroyed government army units.
Amadi is 160 km (100 miles) west of Juba. An outpost at Jambo, which the SPLA said it had captured on Thursday, is 80 km (50 miles) northwest of the government-held southern capital.
The rebel claims could not be independently confirmed.
Arman said the push on Juba, which is heavily-defended, was coordinated with offensives in the east and northeast.
A coalition of forces under the command of SPLA leader John Garang is fighting to overthrow Khartoum's Islamist government in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) rebel coalition.
In mid-March the SPLA captured the southern town of Yei, 160 km (100 miles) southwest of Juba.

Garang on Tuesday said the NDA seized several northeastern districts in an offensive aimed at cutting the road between Khartoum and Sudan's main link to the outside world at Port Sudan on the Red Sea.
The government has dismissed rebel claims to control one of the districts, Aqiq, and has accused Eritrea and Ethiopia of sending troops to fight alongside rebels in the north and northeast.
Both countries deny helping the rebels, as does Uganda, which is accused by Khartoum of backing the SPLA in the south.
Since 1983 the SPLA has fought for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. The NDA says it aims to trigger a popular uprising in Khartoum.
